To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Shape intervention was associated with a significantly greater decrease in weight and a significantly lower increase in waist circumference in black women who were at risk for obesity compared with those who received usual care.

a 12-month, community-based, primary care intervention to prevent weight gain among overweight and obese black women was effective in reducing weight and improving diet and physical activity behaviors.

a modestly intensive, culturally appropriate, team-based intervention delivered to overweight and obese premenopausal African-American women by primary care physicians and community health educators can prevent weight gain for 18 months.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prevention of weight gain in black women, an important health issue because of the high prevalence of obesity among black women and the associated risk for chronic disease.
how people think and act when faced with decisions that have consequences for their own health.
the development of effective weight gain prevention programs for Black women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study shows that a community-based weight maintenance program for black women was effective in reducing weight gain over 18 months.
the evidence is insufficient to recommend for or against the use of any dietary supplements for weight loss in children or adolescents.
the evidence does not support the use of the drug for the treatment of obesity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is not just about weight loss, it is about weight gain prevention, and it is about health and well-being. —Linda S. Bennett
we are not only interested in the prevention of weight gain, but also in the promotion of health.
we need to do a lot more to help patients lose weight, and to help them keep it off.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a modest weight gain intervention is feasible, acceptable, and effective for African American women.
it is possible to prevent weight gain among African American women, a high-risk group for obesity, diabetes, and heart disease.
we can help women avoid weight gain, and this may be an important first step in preventing obesity-related health consequences in high-risk populations.
